title: Can coastal fishing zones protect Africa's artisanal fishers?
summary: New radar data shows that protected nearshore fishing zones can successfully keep industrial vessels out of African coastal waters, boosting fish stocks and small-scale catches without cutting industrial fishing overall.

title: Does asking communities to contribute to development projects improve impact and cost-effectiveness?
summary: A field experiment in Bangladesh finds that requiring cash contributions for safe drinking-water wells sharply reduces take-up and impact, whereas labour contributions work about as well as no contribution at all – yet either requirement leaves the programme less cost-effective.

title: Using mobile phones to support teachers, parents, and students
summary: A new J-PAL Policy Insight reviewing 30 studies across low- and middle-income countries finds that mobile phones can improve student learning, teacher performance, and parental engagement, but only when paired with interactive, two-way pedagogy rather than one-way messaging.

title: Should workers or managers decide who gets rewarded?
summary: A field experiment with Indian carpet firms finds that letting workers vote on rewards boosts attendance but enables collusion, while giving managers discretion boosts output but damages workplace cohesion.
